newsitem.title: FRANCE: Boeing says McDonnell merger talk premature -paper.
newsitem.headline: Boeing says McDonnell merger talk premature -paper.

text.p: The president of Boeing Commercial Airplane Group (BCAG) said on Wednesday it was too early to consider merger prospects with McDonnell Douglas, Le Figaro reported on Wednesday.
Ron Woodard was asked in an interview whether BCAG, a unit of Boeing Co, envisaged a merger and said, "It is far too early. Let us first get our cooperation programme on its feet."

Boeing and McDonnell Douglas on Tuesday said they had agreed to collaborate on future Boeing wide-body aircraft, including new versions of the 747 jumbo jet, the 747-500X and 747-600X. The deal is expected to put pressure on Airbus Industrie.

Woodard said the pact related exclusively to technical and development aspects of the "stretched" 747 and only encompassed the civilian businesses of the two companies. Both firms are heavily involved in the military sector.
"To go from there to talking about a merger is a step I will not make," he told the newspaper.
Woodard himself took the initiative to approach McDonnell Douglas after the latter lost a vital competition for the U.S. Joint Strike Fighter (JSF) on November 18, he said.
The timing was all the more appropriate as MDD had in October announced it was dropping plans to develop the MD-XX wide-body passenger jet, he said.

Boeing currently has seven planes under development and will soon add a larger 767-400 and the two new 747 derivatives, he said. That meant Boeing's engineers are very busy and McDonnell Douglas' collaboration would allow Boeing to cope with it its workload.
Launch decisions on the new 747 models could be made "without problems within six months," he added.

Airbus Industrie is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
Airbus is working on its own project for a 550-seater plane, the A3XX, to rival the Boeing monopoly in large capacity jets.
